newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss see no need for new wartime probe by Jews.
newsitem.headline: Swiss see no need for new wartime probe by Jews.

text.p: A Swiss envoy and Jewish community leaders on Tuesday described a plan by world Jewish groups for a special commission to shadow Switzerland's inquiry into its financial role in World War Two as unnecessary.

Special ambassador Thomas Borer, head of a Swiss government task force on dormant Holocaust-era accounts, and the Swiss Jewish Federation (SIG) said an international historians' panel formed by the Berne government could hold an independent probe.
Jewish Agency president Avraham Burg and the World Jewish Congress on Monday urged creation of their own body in partnership with Israel to oversee the Berne commission.
But Borer and SIG vice-president Thomas Lyssy said the panel created by Berne in December was sufficiently independent.

Borer recalled that the Berne commission headed by Zurich professor Jean-Francois Bergier included four scholars from Israel, the United States and Poland. Three of the nine members, including one Swiss, were Jewish.

"For me, this is a guarantee that the commission will make its historical judgments independently," Borer told Swiss public radio DRS. "I regret the distrust that is apparent in Mr Burg's words," he added.

Lyssey said he was not happy at Burg's call. "If the Jewish Agency has documents it believes are worth examining, then we believe it would make sense to share their knowledge with the Bergier commission and cooperate rather than taking a separate path," Lyssey told DRS.
Burg's Jewish Agency and World Jewish Congress secretary general Israel Singer said in a statement they were concerned that "there could be an attempt to rewrite history" by the Bergier commission.

Bergier's panel was given a broad mandate by the Swiss government to establish the facts of neutral Switzerland's wartime financial role, including the scope of Jewish wealth stashed in Swiss banks to avoid Nazi seizure, Swiss purchases of Nazi gold and banking and business ties with Hitler's Germany.

It is separate from a commission set up last May by Swiss banks and world Jewish groups to sift Swiss bank records for Jewish accounts left ownerless by the Holocaust and double-check the banks' efforts to find heirs to the money.

That commission, chaired by former U.S. central bank chief Paul Volcker, includes Burg as one of three Jewish members who sit alongside three represenatives of the banks. The Volcker commission is due to meet next on January 30 and 31 in Zurich.

Both the Volcker and Bergier commissions were created under pressure led by the World Jewish Congress for an accounting of accounts left by Holocaust victims as well as swiss trade and financial ties with Nazi Germany. Six million Jews died in the Holocaust at the hands of the Nazis during World war Two.
